text:
Maya: trying to onboard a new user with the sample app and hitting weird runtime issues on edge (Vercel).
Sam: ugh, what error?
Maya: import fails: "Cannot find module 'redwood-js-sdk'" but only in edge. node build works fine.
Jordan: probably conditional exports / ESM vs CJS resolution issue. Edge runtimes prefer ESM.
Maya: yes, package.json has both builds but the sample uses `require('redwood-js-sdk')` in the serverless adapter shim.
Priya: if sample is CommonJS but deployed to edge, bundler might inline/transform weirdly. What does our `exports` look like?
Maya: current exports: 
```json
{
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
Sam: that format alone is ok, but for Node + Edge + bundlers you want conditional exports. something like: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
Jordan: careful: `types` inside `exports` is not widely supported. better to keep top-level `types` + `exports` mapping for runtime. TS will read `types`.
Priya: also need a small ESM-compatible entry that doesn't use Node built-ins (fs, path) so it runs on edge. We had a bug where the ESM entry re-exported a file that pulled in `node-fetch` which breaks on edge.
Maya: aha — that matches the stack. The edge bundle looked for `node-fetch` poly that fails at runtime.
Sam: quick patch: add an `./edge` subpath in exports that pointers to a tiny ESM shim optimized for edge: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./edge": "./dist/esm/edge-entry.js"
}
```
Jordan: then sample app can `import sdk from 'redwood-js-sdk/edge'` when running in edge. We should make that transparent: runtime-detecting adapter in sample.
Priya: another sticky area: typings. Consumers using `import type` want accurate d.ts paths. We should ensure `dist/types/index.d.ts` doesn't reference `../cjs` paths. Keep type-only index that re-exports types-only.
Maya: any short-term workaround for onboarding users now? I can update the sample app to import `redwood-js-sdk/edge` conditionally.
Sam: yeah, in sample add this snippet: 
```js
const isEdge = typeof WebSocket !== 'undefined' && process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge';
const sdkPath = isEdge ? 'redwood-js-sdk/edge' : 'redwood-js-sdk';
const SDK = await import(sdkPath);
```
Jordan: also add a note in README and a small CI smoke test that runs the sample in an edge-like environment (wrangler or vercel dev) to catch this earlier.
Priya: FYI there was also an auth/retry mismatch: the ESM edge shim was bypassing our Node retry wrapper, so auth token refresh logic didn't retry correctly. Need to unify the auth layer across entrypoints.
Maya: do we have a thin common core that both cjs and esm delegate to?
Sam: we do, but our build pipeline generated two different bundles with duplicated auth code. We should export the auth core as `auth/core.js` and import it from both bundles to avoid drift.
Jordan: ops plan: 1) add `./edge` export + edge-entry that only references browser-safe deps; 2) refactor auth into single core module and reference from both builds; 3) update sample to conditional import; 4) add CI smoke for edge runtime.
Maya: I'll open a PR for sample + docs.
Priya: I'll take the package.json/exports refactor. Sam/Jordan can help with auth core.
DevExBot: Deploy check: added `devex/smoke/edge-sample` job to the queue for the PRs. :rocket:
Maya: thanks all — this should fix the onboarding friction. I'll ping if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
